reconstructed_theorem_text: For every pair of real sequences a, delta : N -> R and every natural number n, if |a(i+1) - a(i)| <= delta(i) for every natural number i with i < n, then |a(n) - a(0)| <= sum_(i=0)^(n-1) delta(i). The sum is finite and ranges over precisely the indices 0 through n-1; for n = 0 it is the empty sum 0 and the conclusion is 0 <= 0. No condition is imposed on delta outside this index range, and no separate nonnegativity assumption is required.
objects: Two real sequences a and delta and a natural number n; the adjacent increments a(i+1)-a(i); the endpoint difference a(n)-a(0); and the finite sum of delta over indices below n.
domains: a : N -> R, delta : N -> R, and n : N. Absolute values, differences, inequalities, and the finite sum are ordinary real operations. Finset.range n is exactly {i in N : i < n}.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over all a, delta, and n. The premise is universal over natural indices i satisfying i < n. The conclusion concerns the endpoints 0 and n for that same n.
assumptions: For every natural number i with i < n, |a(i+1)-a(i)| <= delta(i). No further assumption is imposed.
conclusion: |a(n)-a(0)| <= sum over i in Finset.range n of delta(i), equivalently the sum over i = 0,...,n-1.
scopes: Only increments with indices below n are controlled. No premise concerns delta at or beyond n. The premise implies delta(i) >= 0 for i < n, but this is not an added hypothesis. n = 0 is permitted, with an empty premise and the conclusion 0 <= 0. This is a deterministic finite statement, with no probability measure, infinite sum, or limit.
constant_dependencies: Every summand has coefficient 1, and there is no additional multiplicative constant. Dependence on n is through the endpoint and the finite index range alone.
